source_text.docs/agents/requirements.yaml REQ-001a (: ...Replace the static language switcher already present in src/components/landing/Nav.tsx (the <div className="lang"> block with RU/UZ/EN spans...) with a working switcher between ru and uz only (drop the non-functional EN option -- no English locale is in scope)...

task.description:
GitHub issue #3 ('translate to en') asks for an English version of the site. This is NOT a bug -- REQ-001a explicitly dropped English from scope ('no English locale is in scope') when it built the ru/uz i18n mechanism, so there is no existing requirement specifying English-locale behavior. Per ORCHESTRATOR.md's decision tree this is a new-feature request: WF-01 (draft + validate) then WF-02 (implement), not WF-03.

Current state (verified before this dispatch): locales are ['ru','uz'], defaultLocale 'ru' (src/i18n/routing.ts). messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json exist with the full landing-page copy (~177 keys per REQ-002's closeout); there is no messages/en.json. Nav.tsx's switcher currently offers RU/UZ only (the EN option was deliberately removed by REQ-001a). The design system readme's brand voice principle #6 commits to 'Multilingual by default -- Russian, Uzbek, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tajik, English -- equal weight', so adding English is realizing an existing brand commitment, not new scope invention (same framing REQ-ANALYST used for the original uz work).

Draft this as one or more requirements sized to one agent turn each per WF-01 Step 1c (split with depends_on chaining if the routing/switcher-mechanism work and the actual translation-content work don't fit one turn together -- this project's own precedent from issue #2 split exactly this way: REQ-001a mechanism -> REQ-001b remaining-copy-extraction -> REQ-002 real translations). Concretely this likely means:
1. A FRONTEND-DEV-owned requirement: add 'en' to the locales list in src/i18n/routing.ts, decide correct ordering/defaultLocale handling (defaultLocale stays 'ru' unless you find a stated reason to change it -- do not silently change default-locale behavior), restore a working EN control in Nav.tsx's switcher (three-way ru/uz/en), and seed messages/en.json with every key from messages/ru.json (English translations, or Russian-verbatim placeholders if you decide to split translation quality into its own follow-up requirement the way REQ-002 was split from REQ-001a/b -- your call, state the reasoning).
2. If you split out translation quality: a CONTENT-BA-owned requirement, depends_on the first, producing real English copy for every messages/en.json key following content_ba_guide.md's voice rules, explicitly stating how domain vocabulary (Event/Chapter/CFP/etc., already English in ru/uz per precedent) is handled now that the target locale IS English (this is a genuinely new question the uz/ru precedent doesn't settle -- decide and state it, don't leave it implicit).

Read docs/agents/requirements.yaml in full first (existing schema + the REQ-001a/b/REQ-002 entries as the direct precedent for how this exact kind of work was split and worded last time). Read docs/agents/anti-patterns.md and docs/agents/decisions/ for anything relevant. Verify current locale/message-catalog state yourself rather than trusting this summary (open src/i18n/routing.ts, messages/ru.json, Nav.tsx) per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §1.1.
acceptance_criteria: One or more new entries appended to docs/agents/requirements.yaml (next sequential REQ-NNN ids after REQ-002) following the exact existing schema, status: pending
If split into multiple requirements, the later one(s) depends_on the earlier one(s) correctly

Each requirement has >=2 concrete, testable acceptance criteria (no vague language -- e.g. 'every key in messages/en.json has a non-empty value, verified by a diff/script against messages/ru.json's key set', not 'translations look good')
The requirement(s) state explicitly what defaultLocale remains and why (do not silently imply a change to 'ru' as default)

If translation quality is split into its own requirement, that requirement explicitly decides and states the domain-vocabulary-in-English question (a genuinely new decision not settled by the ru/uz precedent)
Neither requirement contradicts REQ-001a's done status/description (i.e. do not describe this as 'fixing' or 'redoing' REQ-001a -- it is additive: a new locale REQ-001a explicitly scoped out)

Sized to one agent turn per requirement per WF-01 Step 1c -- split further if the routing+switcher+catalog-seeding+real-translation work doesn't fit one turn together, following the REQ-001a/b/REQ-002 precedent

result.summary: Drafted two new requirements appended to docs/agents/requirements.yaml: REQ-003 (FRONTEND-DEV, depends_on [REQ-001a, REQ-001b]) adds 'en' to src/i18n/routing.ts's locales array and seeds messages/en.json with Russian-duplicated placeholders; REQ-004 (CONTENT-BA, depends_on [REQ-003]) writes real English copy into messages/en.json and decides the domain-vocabulary-in-English question explicitly. Verified current state myself before drafting rather than trusting the handoff's summary: src/i18n/routing.ts has locales=['ru','uz'], defaultLocale='ru'; messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json each have exactly 177 leaf keys with identical key sets (verified with a Python key-flattening script, not just line counts); src/i18n/request.ts's locale-resolution/fallback logic is locale-count-agnostic and needs no change. Found the handoff's artifacts_in/source_text description of the switcher was stale: the RU/UZ-only inline <div className="lang"> block in Nav.tsx described by REQ-001a's text has since been extracted into src/components/landing/LocaleSwitcher.tsx, which now iterates routing.locales generically with no hardcoded per-locale JSX -- meaning REQ-003's mechanism work is simpler than the handoff assumed (adding 'en' to routing.locales alone produces a working three-way switcher; no switcher code change needed). Recorded this finding explicitly in REQ-003's description and in issues below rather than silently carrying the stale framing forward. Read docs/agents/anti-patterns.md and both decisions/ records (0001 full-pipeline-adopted, 0002 content-ba-owns-message-catalogs) -- 0002 confirms CONTENT-BA writing directly into messages/en.json (REQ-004) is consistent with established precedent, not a new call. Confirmed the YAML parses cleanly via a Python yaml.safe_load check and that REQ-003/REQ-004's depends_on ids (REQ-001a, REQ-001b, REQ-003) all reference existing entries -- no orphaned references. Did not validate the requirements myself -- that is REQ-VALIDATOR's job per WF-01 Step 2.

issues.description: This handoff's context.source_text and context.artifacts_in described the locale switcher as still living inline in src/components/landing/Nav.tsx per REQ-001a's original wording ('the <div className="lang"> block with RU/UZ/EN spans'). That is stale: the switcher was extracted into src/components/landing/LocaleSwitcher.tsx at some point after REQ-001a, and it now renders generically from routing.locales with no hardcoded locale list. REQ-003's description states the verified current state and adjusts its scope of work accordingly (no LocaleSwitcher.tsx change required, only a fallback instruction to fix and record if implementation finds otherwise). Flagging so ORCH updates the source-of-truth framing for future dispatches referencing this component.

result.next_action: Route to REQ-VALIDATOR (WF-01 Step 2) to validate REQ-003 and REQ-004.
